findings.title: Multiline full_log smuggles fake Rule:/Alert headers into GetAlertData, yielding integrator shell RCE via ruledescription/alertlocation
findings.description: OS_Log writes lf->full_log into alerts.log with embedded newlines intact (%.1256s). GetAlertData then re-parses any subsequent line starting with 'Rule: ' or '** Alert' as structured fields, overwriting comment, and with a short header-reset sequence also location and alertid. ossec-integratord interpolates al_data->comment and al_data->location into ruledescription='%s' and alertlocation='%s' with no sanitization (unlike alertlog/srcip). Slack and PagerDuty integrations source that file as shell. A registered agent can send a secure event whose log contains a BAD_WORDS token (rule 1002) plus a smuggled Rule line such as Rule: 1002 (level 7) -> 'x'; cmd; y='', or a full mini-alert that resets location. This is distinct from location-suffix RCE and from description_append OpenSCAP title RCE: the agent controls the log body only, and any logged rule works.
findings.impact: Remote command execution as ossecm on the manager whenever Slack or PagerDuty (or a custom integration that sources the alert file) is enabled. That user can read manager state, alerts, and keys under the OSSEC tree and is a foothold to further compromise the HIDS.
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator enables Slack or PagerDuty integration.
2. Attacker has a registered agent key.
3. Agent sends a LOCALFILE_MQ-shaped secure payload whose log is e.g. error failed\nRule: 1002 (level 7) -> 'x'; id; y='' (or a full ** Alert / date / Rule mini-block to also overwrite location).
4. Rule 1002 matches BAD_WORDS; OS_Log writes the multiline full_log into alerts.log.
5. integratord GetAlertData overwrites comment (and optionally location); writes /tmp/<name>-*.alert with ruledescription='x'; id; y=''.
6. integrations/slack or pagerduty runs . $ALERTFILE, executing the injected command as ossecm.
findings.remediation: Stop sourcing alert files as shell; pass fields via argv/env and parse as data. In GetAlertData, once the real Rule: line is parsed, treat all further lines as log body only (do not re-match Rule:/Src IP:/User:/** Alert). Strip CR/LF from full_log before OS_Log, or reject log lines that mimic alert metadata. Sanitize comment and location the same way alertlog/srcip are sanitized before writing integrator temp files.
findings.distinctness: Different root cause and trigger than integrator location-suffix RCE and description_append OpenSCAP comment RCE. Requires only a default logged rule plus newlines in full_log; no OpenSCAP ruleset and no quote in the agent location suffix.

findings.title: os_dbd interpolates unsanitized alertid after GetAlertData header smuggling from full_log
findings.description: Both MySQL and PostgreSQL alert INSERT paths embed al_data->alertid in single-quoted SQL with no osdb_escapestr. alertid is normally manager-generated (time.ftell), but GetAlertData will overwrite it when full_log contains a smuggled '** Alert <id>:' line after a parse-error reset clears the prior date/location. A registered agent that triggers any logged alert can therefore place SQL metacharacters into alertid. PostgreSQL PQexec accepts stacked statements; MySQL is vulnerable to quote-break within the INSERT depending on client flags.
findings.impact: When ossec-dbd is enabled, an authenticated agent can perform SQL injection against the alert database via alertid, including stacked statements on PostgreSQL, corrupting or reading data allowed to the dbd role.
findings.attack_path:
1. Operator enables ossec-dbd (MySQL or PostgreSQL).
2. Attacker has a registered agent key.
3. Agent sends a log that fires a default rule (e.g. rule 1002) whose full_log contains: a junk '** Alert' line, a line that forces GetAlertData l_error (clearing date), then '** Alert 1'; DROP TABLE alert;--: mail - g', a date/location line, a Rule line, and a log line.
4. GetAlertData returns alertid=1'; DROP TABLE alert;--.
5. OS_Alert_InsertDB snprintf's that value into the INSERT; osdb_query_insert/PQexec runs the injected SQL.
findings.remediation: Call osdb_escapestr on alertid (or use parameterized queries). Reject non [0-9.] alertids. Fix GetAlertData so log-body lines cannot reopen '** Alert' / Rule: parsing after the first Rule line.
findings.distinctness: Already-reported dbd SQLi covers unsanitized location and PostgreSQL srcip/dstip from decoders. This is a different column (alertid), normally trusted, made attacker-controlled only through read-alert field smuggling; MySQL is also affected for this field.
